bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- The Rs. 182 cr write-off is the *reason* reported PAT collapsed to Rs. 5 cr — purely accounting/non-cash, and it lowers future Filmistan project cost (margin-positive later). Easy to misread as operational weakness.
- Filmistan structuring: outright land (Aspen/Kamanwala) + tenancy via Filmistan Pvt Ltd (WoS) → demerged/merged into Arkade (order Mar '26) to consolidate ownership.
- Ashok Nagar MOU signed literally the evening before the call ("last evening") — fresh pipeline add.
- Mgmt implicitly distinguishes EBITDA "targeting 25%" (MD) vs "stabilize 27–28%" (CFO) — a 2–3pt aspiration gap.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- "Healthy balance sheet, disciplined capital allocation, and low-leverage approach, enabling the company to capitalize on emerging redevelopment and greenfield opportunities."
- Net debt of INR 50 million and net debt-to-equity of 0.01x as at June 30, 2026; the net debt/equity series reads 0.17 (FY24), -0.03 (FY25), 0.08 (FY26) and 0.01 (Q1-FY27).
- Networth of INR 3,236 Mn (FY24), 8,839 Mn (FY25) and 8,822 Mn (FY26); ROCE and ROE shown as 52.66%/46.92% (FY24), 32.31%/25.99% (FY25) and 19.64%/21.23% (FY26), stated to be calculated after adjusting for exceptional items.
- Cash flow statement shows net IPO funds of INR 4,070 Mn in FY25 and a first dividend payout of INR 36 Mn in FY26 (nil in FY24 and FY25).
- Expected cash flow potential of INR 1,40,710 Mn, comprising pending collections from launched sold projects INR 5,590 Mn, cash flow potential from launched unsold INR 6,968 Mn, unsold inventory from completed projects INR 111 Mn, pending collections from completed sold projects INR 191 Mn, and unlaunched projects INR 1,27,850 Mn.

bull_bear.body:
- In-house project management across the full lifecycle — dedicated construction, design, procurement, QA/QC, CRM and sales & marketing teams give end-to-end execution control and support timely delivery

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic and single-market concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region — The entire ongoing and upcoming portfolio sits in MMR micro-markets and Thane, so any MMR-specific demand, pricing, approval or regulatory shock hits the whole business at once. The MD&A itself flags that redevelopment execution in MMR is complex, requiring multiple approvals, regulatory clearances and stakeholder coordination, which extends project timelines and adds execution risk.
- Financial risk from leverage in a capital-intensive development cycle — Management states that Indian real estate developers must avoid excessive leverage because high debt hurts profitability and can trigger broader market price inflation. Mitigation is prudent capital allocation, an optimal debt-equity mix, strengthened cash flow planning, diversified funding, close working-capital monitoring, periodic financial risk assessments and cost control.
- Macroeconomic slowdown weakening housing demand — A broader economic slowdown or global macro uncertainty could reduce domestic consumption, raise unemployment and cut investment activity, directly weakening property demand and sectoral growth. The Company mitigates by monitoring macro indicators, strengthening liquidity and aligning project launches with prevailing demand conditions.
- Interest-rate reversal raising mortgage costs and project funding costs — The RBI's accommodative stance is described as vulnerable to reversal if inflation flares on supply-chain disruption or high public spending. Rising rates and mortgage costs dampen housing demand and discourage the borrowing needed to fund future projects. Mitigation is a prudent fixed/floating borrowing mix, periodic refinancing, rate monitoring and adequate liquidity.
- Construction material cost and supply-chain disruption — Geopolitical tension in the Middle East and Eastern Europe threatens the stability of steel, cement and glass costs and can delay shipping and energy routes. Developers must either absorb the higher input cost, compressing margins, or pass it to buyers and risk lower demand. Mitigation is long-term supplier relationships, supplier diversification, procurement planning, commodity price monitoring and inventory of critical materials.
- Environmental regulation, pollution controls and climate transition risk — Stringent environmental regulation and pollution-control action in MMR — including closure of non-compliant ready-mix concrete plants and stricter enforcement — has caused project execution delays and raised compliance burden. The BRSR materiality table classifies Climate Change as a risk with negative financial implications through extreme weather events, operational disruption, rising compliance requirements and evolving stakeholder expectations; mitigation is climate-resilient design, periodic climate risk and vulnerability assessments, disaster preparedness and business-continuity planning.
- Specialised workforce and talent shortage constraining scale-up — The industry faces a shortage of the specialised talent needed for large-scale expansion, with a gap between the available labour pool and the technical skills required. Since the Company engages no site workers directly on its payroll and depends on contractor labour, sustained growth depends on scaling employability. Mitigation is talent acquisition, training and upskilling, retention initiatives, partnerships with educational and vocational institutions, and process automation.
- Business ethics, governance and compliance failure — The BRSR materiality table identifies Business Ethics and Governance as a risk with negative financial implications, citing the potential impact of unethical practices, regulatory non-compliance, fraud, corruption and governance lapses on reputation, stakeholder confidence, legal compliance and long-term sustainability. Mitigation is a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy covering employees, directors and business partners, periodic compliance monitoring, internal controls and internal audit.
- Data protection and cyber security exposure — Identified in the BRSR materiality table as a risk with negative financial implications, arising from cyberattacks, data breaches, unauthorised access and technology disruption affecting business continuity, stakeholder trust, regulatory compliance and reputation.
- Concentration of asset value in the acquired tenancy right, already impaired in FY26 — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to the group's tenancy-right asset arising from the Filmistan Private Limited acquisition and the NCLT-approved demerger of its rental business; the Group recognised an impairment/diminution of Rs 18,217.09 Lakhs on that asset in the year ended 31 March 2026 and treated it as an allowable deduction under the Income-tax Act with no corresponding tax provision, so the tax treatment remains an open exposure. The opinion is not modified in respect of the matter.

business.body:
- Described as a "Leading MMR Developer with Inhouse Project Management", specialising in premium residential development across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region with a strategic focus on high-demand micro-markets.

- Snapshot claims a 40+ year legacy of excellence, 32 projects completed, 5,500+ homes delivered and 5.5 Mn Sq.Ft + area delivered; the completed portfolio slide splits the 32 projects into 18 greenfield and 14 redevelopment.
- Industry case for MMR: India's largest residential market by sales volume (97,188 units in 2025 vs 55,373 Bengaluru), infrastructure-led growth (metro, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Atal Setu/MTHL), and redevelopment at ~60-65% of Mumbai's residential development pipeline.
- Awards cited include Project of the Year (Arkade Earth), Iconic Residential Developer, and Iconic Luxury Residential Project of the Year (Arkade Aura); issuer rating IND-RA BBB+, ISO-9001-2015 and ISO-45001-2018 certified.

- [Business development] Successfully advanced business development through strategic land acquisitions across key MMR micro-markets; earlier journey milestones include the Filmistan Pvt Ltd acquisition (4-acre Goregaon, projected GDV Rs. 3,500 cr), Thane entry (Rs. 1,900 cr), a Bhandup 3.5-acre MOU (Rs. 1,000 cr) and rights to redevelop 13.5 acres in the western suburbs (Rs. 4,500 cr).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Arkade Developers develops residential and, to a lesser extent, commercial property across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, managing the entire project lifecycle from conceptualisation and planning through approvals, construction, marketing and post-possession customer support with in-house teams. The business runs on two core segments: New Development Projects, where land parcels are acquired for greenfield residential schemes, and Redevelopment Projects, where existing buildings and housing societies are rebuilt into upgraded residential developments. It sells primarily to end-user homebuyers in Mumbai's eastern, western and central suburbs and Thane, and has extended into adjacent homeownership services through Arkade FinRoof (home-loan assistance) and Assist 360 (property and facility management).

outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

outlook.body:
- Ride the premiumisation wave in Mumbai residential by moving up the value chain into larger, design-led and uber-luxury developments such as Filmistan Studios
- Expand the redevelopment portfolio across established micro-markets, moving the current ~65% greenfield / 35% redevelopment mix towards a balanced 50:50 over the long term
- Maintain a disciplined, asset-light operating model with low leverage (debt-equity ratio of 0.11 in FY26), healthy cash flows and efficient capital use to preserve flexibility for new opportunities
- Strengthen presence in Mumbai's emerging central/eastern corridor — Mulund and Bhandup — where infrastructure investment is driving residential demand; the 14,363 sq. metre Bhandup West land parcel adds another greenfield project
- Sustain execution advantage by securing approvals prior to launch and coordinating legal, planning, procurement and construction teams to deliver within and often ahead of committed timelines
- Run an IRR-driven project selection approach that favours projects executable quickly, supporting faster revenue recognition and steady cash generation
- Operate a two-layer execution platform: in-house teams for construction, design, procurement, QA/QC, CRM and sales, supported by a specialist ecosystem of design, landscape, structural and lighting consultants
- Extend the customer relationship beyond handover through FinRoof (integrated home-loan assistance) and Assist 360 (integrated property and facility management), plus the Arkade Family First App and Family First Circle referral programme
- Embed sustainability through the proprietary REST Advantage framework (Rejuvenation, Eco-friendliness, Sustainability, Technology) at every stage of design and execution
- Build brand salience in core redevelopment micro-markets, including securing the branding and naming rights for the Bangur Nagar Metro Station (now Arkade Bangur Nagar)
- Simplify the group structure — acquire Filmistan Private Limited outright and demerge its rental business into the Company as part of the overall strategy for the optimum running, growth and development of the Company in real estate
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Arkade's expansion is land-and-project acquisition rather than plant capex. The Company reports a development pipeline of roughly Rs 12,800 crore GDV across about 4.25 million sq ft of saleable carpet area, on top of 5.5+ mn sq ft already developed, 2+ mn sq ft under development and 32 projects delivered. Under 'Strategies for the future' it plans eight new project launches across Goregaon, Thane, Borivali, Malad and Santacruz in the MMR, with a combined projected GDV of over Rs 9,225 crore. FY26 additions were: the Filmistan land parcel at Goregaon West (greenfield, ~4.11-4.25 acres, projected GDV Rs 3,500 crore, 8,87,548 sq ft saleable carpet), which takes the Company into the uber-luxury segment; a 6.28-acre freehold parcel at Kasarvadavali, Thane bought for Rs 172.48 crore including stamp duty (projected GDV Rs 2,000 crore, RERA saleable area 9.26 lakh sq ft), marking entry into the Thane market; an MoU to acquire 100% of Woollen and Textile Industries Ltd for Rs 148 crore, covering a 3.5-3.55 acre mixed residential-commercial parcel at Bhandup West (projected GDV Rs 1,000 crore, 4,26,000 sq ft); the Ashok Nagar cluster redevelopment at Kandivali East consolidating 9 housing societies on ~3 acres (projected GDV Rs 1,100 crore, ~3.25 lakh sq ft RERA carpet); and the Jal Ratna Deep society redevelopment at Goregaon West on 1.1 acres (projected GDV Rs 350 crore, 86,810 sq ft). The stated upcoming-project roster also includes Anand Nagar, Dahisar East (6,76,000 sq ft, Rs 1,700 crore GDV), Nutan Ayojan, Malad West (2,33,000 sq ft, Rs 740 crore), Satya Shripal, Borivali West (2,39,100 sq ft, Rs 800 crore), Rani Sati, Malad West (2,11,940 sq ft, Rs 725 crore), Jumbo Darshan, Andheri East (1,04,100 sq ft, Rs 385 crore), Apna Ghar, Andheri West (92,815 sq ft, Rs 375 crore) and Maheshwari Niwas, Santacruz West (41,140 sq ft, Rs 210 crore); ongoing projects include Arkade Rare, Bhandup West (3,13,070 sq ft) and Arkade Nest, Mulund West (2,60,989 sq ft). Geographically the strategy is an eastern- and central-corridor push into Bhandup, Mulund and Thane alongside the established western suburbs, and cumulative redevelopment rights of 13.5 acres in the western suburbs with a projected GDV of Rs 4,500 crore. The Company also states it is systematically augmenting front-end project-execution and sales teams to carry the higher project volumes, and expanded its service footprint by incorporating Assist 360 Facility Management Private Limited (3 December 2025) for integrated facility management. Financing is deliberately asset-light: redevelopment priority and selective land acquisition to minimise upfront capital expenditure, with the Company describing a zero net debt position; the entire Rs 41,000 lakh of IPO proceeds (Rs 25,000 lakh to development expenses and Rs 13,007.50 lakh to land acquisition and general corporate purposes) had been fully utilised by 31 March 2026.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Mumbai's residential market is shifting decisively towards premium and lifestyle-led housing: homes above Rs 1 crore now account for nearly half of all registrations and the Rs 2-5 crore band is the largest contributor to market activity
- Over 1.5 lakh property registrations in Mumbai in 2025 — the highest in more than a decade — with demand driven largely by end users
- The MMR luxury segment now commands a 44% share of sales by area, up sharply from 31% in FY21, while the sub-Rs 1 crore affordable segment keeps shrinking
- MMR inventory has compressed to a historic-low 'years to sell' of 1.2 to 1.4 years as demand outstrips new launches
- Acute scarcity of vacant land in core micro-markets makes urban redevelopment the primary vehicle for high-grade supply — a structural driver of the Company's redevelopment pipeline
- Infrastructure expansion (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, metro network build-out) is broadening the market's centre of gravity and turning Thane, Navi Mumbai and Mira Road into high-velocity residential destinations
- A stable interest-rate corridor — the MPC holding the repo rate at 5.25% under a neutral stance, after a cumulative 125 bps of cuts — removes volatility from borrowing parameters and anchors retail sentiment
- Greenfield development is gaining momentum on planned urban expansion initiatives such as Mumbai 3.0 and rising demand in peripheral locations
- GST rate reduction/GST 2.0 reform is improving homebuyer affordability and cutting rates on major construction inputs, which could improve project viability
- India's GDP is projected at 6.9% for FY 2026-27 with CPI inflation at 4.6%, and the Union Budget 2026-27 proposes a 9% rise in public capex to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, expected to stimulate real estate sales and long-term property value appreciation
- Major listed developers are expected to gain market share through execution and diversification, with demand supported by infrastructure, urban reforms, stable employment and migration
- Watch-item: supply chain disruptions from the West Asia conflict may drive up construction material costs
- Portfolio mix stated at approximately 65% greenfield and 35% redevelopment projects, with a stated long-term goal of a balanced 50:50 mix
- Upcoming project pipeline named across the western, eastern and central suburbs and Thane — Satya Shripal, Nutan Ayojan, Filmistan, Apna Ghar, Maheshwari Niwas, Jal Ratna, Jumbo Darshan, Rani Sati, Ashok Nagar, Woollen Mills, Kasarvadavali and Anand Nagar
- Ongoing projects: Arkade Vistas, Arkade Views, Arkade Rare, Arkade Nest, Arkade Pearl and Arkade Evoke
- Thane land parcel carries a projected Gross Development Value of Rs 2,000 crore on a RERA saleable area of 9.26 lakh sq. ft.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Arkade is an execution-first Mumbai (MMR) residential developer pivoting up the value curve into premium/luxury, funded by a mix of redevelopment rights and outright land buys. FY26 was a "defining year": record quarterly pre-sales (Rs. 303 cr in Q4, +40% YoY) and a marquee, optionality-heavy acquisition (Filmistan, Goregaon West) that anchors a Rs. 3,500 cr GDV uber-luxury project. The reported PAT (Rs. 5 cr FY26) is optically crushed by a one-time Rs. 182 cr non-cash diminution of Filmistan tenancy rights — operationally the business grew. Stated pipeline of ~Rs. 12,000 cr over 5–6 years with a launch-driven (Thane + Filmistan) inflection from FY28. Key debate raised by analysts: 25% CAGR alone only gets cumulative revenue to ~Rs. 5,000–6,000 cr over six years, so the thesis leans heavily on the big-ticket launches converting to "exponential" growth in FY28/FY29.

risks.note: The entire ongoing and upcoming portfolio sits in MMR micro-markets and Thane, so any MMR-specific demand, pricing, approval or regulatory shock hits the whole business at once. The MD&A itself flags that redevelopment execution in MMR is complex, requiring multiple approvals, regulatory clearances and stakeholder coordination, which extends project timelines and adds execution risk.
risks.risk: Geographic and single-market concentration in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region

risks.note: Management states that Indian real estate developers must avoid excessive leverage because high debt hurts profitability and can trigger broader market price inflation. Mitigation is prudent capital allocation, an optimal debt-equity mix, strengthened cash flow planning, diversified funding, close working-capital monitoring, periodic financial risk assessments and cost control.
risks.risk: Financial risk from leverage in a capital-intensive development cycle

risks.note: A broader economic slowdown or global macro uncertainty could reduce domestic consumption, raise unemployment and cut investment activity, directly weakening property demand and sectoral growth. The Company mitigates by monitoring macro indicators, strengthening liquidity and aligning project launches with prevailing demand conditions.

The RBI's accommodative stance is described as vulnerable to reversal if inflation flares on supply-chain disruption or high public spending. Rising rates and mortgage costs dampen housing demand and discourage the borrowing needed to fund future projects. Mitigation is a prudent fixed/floating borrowing mix, periodic refinancing, rate monitoring and adequate liquidity.
risks.risk: Interest-rate reversal raising mortgage costs and project funding costs

risks.note: Geopolitical tension in the Middle East and Eastern Europe threatens the stability of steel, cement and glass costs and can delay shipping and energy routes. Developers must either absorb the higher input cost, compressing margins, or pass it to buyers and risk lower demand. Mitigation is long-term supplier relationships, supplier diversification, procurement planning, commodity price monitoring and inventory of critical materials.
risks.risk: Construction material cost and supply-chain disruption

risks.note: Stringent environmental regulation and pollution-control action in MMR — including closure of non-compliant ready-mix concrete plants and stricter enforcement — has caused project execution delays and raised compliance burden. The BRSR materiality table classifies Climate Change as a risk with negative financial implications through extreme weather events, operational disruption, rising compliance requirements and evolving stakeholder expectations; mitigation is climate-resilient design, periodic climate risk and vulnerability assessments, disaster preparedness and business-continuity planning.
risks.risk: Environmental regulation, pollution controls and climate transition risk

risks.note: The industry faces a shortage of the specialised talent needed for large-scale expansion, with a gap between the available labour pool and the technical skills required. Since the Company engages no site workers directly on its payroll and depends on contractor labour, sustained growth depends on scaling employability. Mitigation is talent acquisition, training and upskilling, retention initiatives, partnerships with educational and vocational institutions, and process automation.
risks.risk: Specialised workforce and talent shortage constraining scale-up

risks.note: The BRSR materiality table identifies Business Ethics and Governance as a risk with negative financial implications, citing the potential impact of unethical practices, regulatory non-compliance, fraud, corruption and governance lapses on reputation, stakeholder confidence, legal compliance and long-term sustainability. Mitigation is a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy covering employees, directors and business partners, periodic compliance monitoring, internal controls and internal audit.
risks.risk: Business ethics, governance and compliance failure
